title: Hybrid connection grooming and progressive read-shed strategy for cross-region caches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Short summary: Implement a hybrid connection grooming layer and progressive read-shedding strategy that preserves critical SLOs during cross-region degradation of Redis and Kafka backends. Goals: maintain 99th-percentile latency < 120ms for read path during partial regional outage; keep error rate < 0.5% for P0 tenants; enable controlled service degradation (soft reads, cached fallbacks, read-tiering) rather than hard failures.

Approach: 1) Introduce a Connection Groomer process in front of downstream clients to dynamically shrink and prioritize connection sets per-tenant and per-region; 2) Implement progressive read-shed profiles (cache-first, approximate reads, stale-reads with TTL extension) selectable by SLO tier; 3) Circuit breaker library with graded trip thresholds and observe-only shadowing for first rollout; 4) Multi-region failover policy that prefers warm read replica, then degraded-mode proxy, then best-effort fallback; 5) Telemetry and runbook: add per-tenant admission metrics, shed-rate, KV hit ratio, and automated alerting tied to SLO burn rates.

Deliverables: connection-groomer service, client library updates, circuit breaker config profiles, console dashboards (per-route shed rate + tenant impact), runbook and canary rollout plan, chaos test scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Connection Groomer reduces connection count under load by at least 40% without increasing P50 latency >10ms. 2) During simulated regional kv outage, progressive shed mode keeps P99 latency <120ms and error-rate increase <=0.5% for P0 tenants. 3) Circuit breaker can be toggled to enforced mode with no data corruption and clear rollback. 4) Dashboards show shed-rate, tenant impact, and canary metrics in console-2026.03.
technical_notes: Groomer algorithm: maintain per-tenant active set prioritized by recent QPS and latency impact; background replenishment to avoid cold-start spikes. Use token-bucket admission with tenant weights and emergency reserve. Read-shed modes: cache-only -> stale-read-with-ttl-bump -> best-effort-stub -> error. Circuit: exponential backoff with hysteresis windows, per-region and per-backend scopes. Persisted state in local embedded store with replication to region control plane for fast failover decisions.
notes: We should coordinate with SRE (pager rota) for chaos windows. Design review scheduled 2026-02-18. Miguel suggested soft-start sampling at 5% of traffic for first canary. Security requested KMS for any persisted tokens.
